circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: The Yas Marina Circuit, a 5. 281 km track on Abu Dhabi's Yas Island designed by Hermann Tilke, has served as the venue for Formula One's season finale since 2009. It was the second Middle Eastern Formula One venue to open, following Bahrain and preceding the circuits in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: Albert Park Circuit winds through the suburbs of Melbourne around its namesake lake as a street-based racing venue. It hosts the Australian Grand Prix each year alongside various supporting motorsport categories and maintains FIA Grade 1 certification standards.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Located in Spielberg, Austria, this 4. 326 km circuit originally opened as the Österreichring and staged the Austrian Grand Prix annually throughout the 1970s and 1980s. Following its reconstruction and renaming, the venue returned to the Formula One calendar in the late 1990s and early 2000s as a shortened circuit.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: Baku City Circuit, situated along Baku Boulevard in Azerbaijan, is a street-based racing venue spanning 6. 003 km, ranking as the fourth-longest track in Formula One. The circuit first hosted a Grand Prix in 2016 under the European Grand Prix designation, before becoming home to the Azerbaijan Grand Prix from 2017 onwards.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Inaugurated in 2004, the Bahrain International Circuit spans 5. 412 km and hosted the first Formula One Grand Prix ever held in the Middle East that same year. Beyond its premier motorsport events, the FIA Grade 1-licensed venue has accommodated various racing series including GP2, drag racing, and 24-hour endurance competitions, with several circuit configurations available for different events.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya stretches 4. 657 kilometers and features a balanced mix of lengthy straightaways and diverse corner configurations that test multiple racing disciplines. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 status and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstand facilities.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: Located in the Walloon region of Belgium near the town of Spa, this 7. 004 km circuit has been a fixture of Formula One racing since 1950, when it featured in the championship's inaugural season. The venue has continuously hosted the Belgian Grand Prix annually since 1985, with only two exceptions in 2003 and 2006.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Montreal's Notre Dame Island, this 4. 361 km circuit in Quebec serves as the home of Canada's Formula One Grand Prix. Beyond F1, the track has accommodated various international racing series including sportscar championships and North American open-wheel and stock car competitions.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: Located in Shanghai's Jiading District, the Shanghai International Circuit serves as China's primary motorsport venue, hosting the Chinese Grand Prix intermittently since 2004, with a hiatus between 2020 and 2023 before resuming in 2024. The facility has expanded its calendar to include electric racing events, beginning with the Shanghai ePrix in 2024.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Located near villages in Northamptonshire, England, Silverstone Circuit hosted the inaugural Formula One World Championship race in 1950 and has been the primary home of the British Grand Prix since 1987, following decades of rotating with other venues. The track remains a cornerstone British motorsport facility, also staging the local MotoGP round.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring near Budapest hosted Formula One's first Eastern Bloc Grand Prix in 1986, constructed in just eight months near a major highway rather than as a street circuit in the city's largest park. This 4. 381 km circuit in Mogyoród became a regular fixture on the championship calendar, with its inaugural race honoring János Drapál, a pioneering Hungarian motorcycle racer.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: Located near Monza in northern Italy, the 5. 793 km Autodromo Nazionale circuit opened in 1922 as mainland Europe's oldest purpose-built racing facility and has hosted the Italian Grand Prix continuously since 1949, earning its nickname "the Temple of Speed" for its characteristic long straights and quick corners. The track's high-speed configuration and prestigious history have made it one of motorsport's most iconic venues.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Suzuka Circuit is a 5. 807 km Japanese motorsports venue situated in Mie Prefecture and operated by Honda Mobilityland. The track, which accommodates 155,000 spectators, primarily hosts Formula One and Super Formula racing events at the international level.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street layout navigating through Paradise, Nevada, alongside the famous Las Vegas Boulevard where major casinos and hotels are located. The track weaves past iconic venues such as MSG Sphere, Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas, incorporating these distinctive landmarks into the racing configuration.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: Located in Mexico City, the 4. 304 km Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez honors two Mexican racing brothers who died in separate accidents during the 1960s and 1970s. The venue has hosted the Formula One Mexican Grand Prix intermittently since 1992, with the race returning to the circuit in 2015 under its current "Mexico City Grand Prix" branding as of 2021.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary circuit constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens that hosts the Miami Grand Prix, which joined the Formula One calendar in 2022. Spanning 3. 363 miles with 19 corners, the track was engineered by Apex Circuit Design and sees qualifying speeds averaging 139 mph.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco winds through the streets of Monte Carlo and La Condamine surrounding Monaco's harbour, covering 3. 337 kilometres. Though technically named after Monaco itself, it is commonly known as the Monte Carlo circuit because most of its layout occupies the Monte Carlo district.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Located in the Dutch coastal dunes near Amsterdam, Circuit Zandvoort is a 4. 259 km track that hosted the Dutch Grand Prix after rejoining the Formula One calendar in 2021. The venue's partnership with Formula One concluded in 2026.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: The Lusail International Circuit, situated near Doha in Qatar, is a 5. 419-kilometer track featuring a 1. 068-kilometer main straight and holding an FIA Grade 1 license.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Located in São Paulo, Brazil, Interlagos is a 4. 309 km circuit that opened in 1940 and was later renamed in 1985 to commemorate the late racing driver José Carlos Pace. The track operates in a counterclockwise direction and features an adjacent kart facility bearing the name of another celebrated Brazilian motorsport figure.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street track situated along the Red Sea waterfront in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, which has hosted the Saudi Arabian Grand Prix since its inaugural Formula One race in 2021. The venue also began hosting a major electric racing championship event starting in 2025.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit winds through downtown Singapore's waterfront, incorporating sections of the city's core urban areas and the Kallang district.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya spans 4. 657 kilometers and features a balanced mix of extended straights and diverse corner configurations, making it suitable for testing all aspects of racing performance. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 certification and accommodates up to 140,700 spectators across its facilities.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: Located in Austin, Texas, the Circuit of the Americas is a 3. 426-mile FIA Grade 1 facility that hosts the Formula One United States Grand Prix alongside NASCAR, MotoGP, and endurance racing competitions. The track has accommodated various international motorsport series over the years, including IndyCar and sports car championships.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon is a Thai and British driver competing for Williams in Formula One under Thailand's flag.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Spanish driver Fernando Alonso competes for Aston Martin in Formula One, where he has captured two world championships with Renault in 2005 and 2006 while securing 32 Grand Prix victories throughout a 23-season career. Beyond Formula One, Alonso has achieved significant success in endurance racing, including two Le Mans victories with Toyota and the 2018-19 FIA World Endurance Championship, making him the sole driver to win both the F1 drivers' title and the world sportscar championship.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Italian driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli joined the Mercedes Formula One team in 2025 and has achieved six Grand Prix victories since entering the sport.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British motorsport competitor currently racing in Formula One with the Haas team.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Gabi Bortoleto, a Brazilian motorsport competitor, currently drives for Audi in Formula One competition.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Finnish driver Valtteri Bottas currently races for Cadillac in Formula One, bringing extensive experience from his 13 seasons in the sport. He achieved two runner-up finishes in the drivers' championship during his time with Mercedes and has accumulated 10 Grand Prix victories throughout his career.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Franco Alejandro Colapinto is an Argentine racing driver currently competing in Formula One with Alpine.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Australian driver Jack Doohan combines reserve duties with Haas in Formula One, where he has participated in seven grands prix between 2024 and 2025, while also racing in the LMP2 category of the European Le Mans Series with Nielsen Racing.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Alpine. He achieved a notable victory at the 2020 Italian Grand Prix while competing for AlphaTauri.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: French-Algerian racing driver Isack Alexandre Hadjar represents France in Formula One competition, currently driving for Red Bull Racing.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton is a British Formula One driver competing for Ferrari who has achieved seven world championship titles, matching Michael Schumacher's record. He holds multiple all-time records including the most race victories, pole positions, and podium finishes in the sport's history.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: Nicolas Hülkenberg is a German Formula One driver currently racing for Audi. Beyond his single-seater commitments, he has achieved significant success in endurance motorsport, notably winning the prestigious 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015 driving for Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson is a New Zealand motorsport competitor who currently drives for Racing Bulls in Formula One.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: Charles Leclerc, a Monégasque driver competing for Ferrari, finished as championship runner-up in 2022 and has accumulated nine Grand Prix victories throughout his nine seasons in Formula One.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Kevin Magnussen is a Danish driver who raced in Formula One across two separate stints, from 2014-2020 and 2022-2024. Currently, he competes as a factory driver for BMW in the FIA World Endurance Championship with WRT, while also taking on a part-time role in NASCAR's Cup Series with Trackhouse Racing.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: British driver Lando Norris claimed the 2025 Formula One World Drivers' Championship while racing for McLaren, adding to his record of 13 Grand Prix victories accumulated over eight seasons in the sport.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon, a French racing driver, currently competes for Haas in Formula One. He previously achieved a notable victory at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix while driving for Alpine.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Mexican driver Sergio "Checo" Pérez competes for Cadillac in Formula One, bringing experience from 15 seasons in the sport. He finished as championship runner-up in 2023 while driving for Red Bull and has accumulated six Grand Prix victories throughout his career.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Oscar Piastri, an Australian driver competing for McLaren in Formula One, has claimed nine Grand Prix victories throughout his four-season tenure in the sport.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Australian driver Daniel Ricciardo competed in Formula One for 14 seasons between 2011 and 2024, securing eight Grand Prix victories during his career. Known by the nickname "the Honey Badger," Ricciardo has since retired from the sport.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: George Russell, a British driver, has achieved seven Grand Prix victories during his eight-year Formula One career with Mercedes.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Carlos Sainz is a Spanish motorsport competitor currently racing for Williams in Formula One, where he has accumulated four race victories throughout his 12-season career in the sport.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: Logan Sargeant is an American driver currently racing in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 category with Proton Competition, following his previous involvement in IMSA's LMP2 class. His Formula One career spanned 2023 to 2024.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian Formula One driver currently racing for Aston Martin in the championship.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Japanese driver Yuki Tsunoda held a Formula One career spanning from 2021 through 2026, during which time he served in reserve roles for both Red Bull Racing and its sister team Racing Bulls.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: Dutch-Belgian driver Max Verstappen races for Red Bull Racing and has secured four consecutive world championships between 2021 and 2024. With 71 Grand Prix victories accumulated over 12 seasons, he stands as one of the sport's most successful drivers.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu is China's sole Formula One competitor to date, having raced in the championship from 2022 through 2024. He currently holds a reserve driver position with Cadillac in the series.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: Operating from Enstone since 2021, this team has competed under the Alpine Racing banner as Renault's works outfit, initially adopting the nameplate to highlight the French manufacturer's sports car division. The team maintained its factory status throughout this period until Renault's withdrawal from the championship concluded at the end of 2025.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin, the British automotive manufacturer, has returned to Formula One competition under the current entity AMR GP Limited, operating as the Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari, the racing arm of the Italian luxury automaker, operates as one of Formula One's most decorated institutions, participating in every World Championship season since the sport's inception in 1950. Renowned by the nickname "the Prancing Horse" after their emblem, the team holds the distinction of being both the longest-continuously competing and most accomplished outfit in the championship's history.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: An American-licensed Formula One outfit founded by NASCAR team owner Gene Haas, the squad entered the sport in 2016 and currently operates under team principal Ayao Komatsu, who took over from Guenther Steiner in early 2024.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: The Swiss engineering firm, established by Peter Sauber in 1970, initially achieved success in endurance racing before joining Formula One as a constructor in 1993. Operating for over three decades in the sport through various iterations, the team competed as one of F1's longest-standing independent chassis manufacturers until ceasing operations in 2025, when its operations and assets were absorbed by Audi to establish their factory team program.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren Racing is a British Formula One outfit headquartered in Woking that competes under Mastercard sponsorship. The team operates as part of the McLaren Group, which is owned by Bahrain's Mumtalakat Holding Company.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has participated in Formula One since 1954 in both ownership and engine supply capacities. The current team, based in Brackley and operating under a German licence, competes as Mercedes-AMG Petronas with ownership shared equally between the Mercedes-Benz Group, Ineos, and Toto Wolff as of January 2022. Mercedes teams are traditionally known as the "Silver Arrows.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One team and constructor based in Faenza that commenced competition in 2024. As one of two constructors operated by Red Bull GmbH, it functions alongside Red Bull Racing, with operational facilities also established near its sister team's headquarters in Milton Keynes.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that began competing in 2024 as part of Red Bull GmbH's two-team operation alongside Red Bull Racing. Headquartered in Faenza with an additional facility near Milton Keynes, the team functions as Red Bull's sister squad within the championship.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing is an Austrian-licensed Formula One team headquartered in England and owned by the Red Bull conglomerate, which also operates Racing Bulls. Founded in 2005 and led by Christian Horner until his 2025 departure, the team is now under Laurent Mekies's management.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering, the British constructor competing in Formula One since 1977, was established by Frank Williams and Patrick Head following the collapse of Williams's previous racing venture. Based in Grove, Oxfordshire, the team has operated as a dedicated F1 constructor and competitor for nearly five decades.
